The $150 in coffees and snacks is a different story: the safer treatment is to leave it out because food consumed while working is considered a personal expense unless you are traveling away from home overnight, while an aggressive position would claim 50% of it on Line 24 as business meals and argue the waiting time makes it necessary—a stance the IRS routinely rejects for local drivers. Your safer draft therefore shows $16,757 on Line 9, $275 on Line 22, $420 on Line 22 (or 9) for parking/tolls, and $1,050 on Line 22 or 25 for phone; the aggressive draft would add roughly $75 on Line 24 and might bump the phone ratio from 80% to the full calculated fraction. Before finalizing, have a tax pro sanity-check any meal deduction because it is a high-risk item for gig drivers and the IRS safe-harbor for meals requires being away from your tax home.
